AUTHOR: D. Zhang
TITLE: A Large Scale Under-Sea Dataset for Marine Observation
VENUE: Global Oceans 2020: Singapore – U.S. Gulf Coast
REGION: SmartBay cabled observatory off Spiddal, Galway Bay, Ireland
DATA: MISSFish: own SmartBay sub-sea observatory video (45 annotated videos, 13,946 frames, 118,830 polygon objects)
V_EV: Sec. III: 'The camera is deployed at 20 meters below the water surface'; videos selected by 'time of the video captured (morning, afternoon, evening and night time)'
D_EV: no statement found (re-trained FgSegNet evaluated without any described train/test split)
R_EV: Sec. IV: 'The IoU score of the pre-trained model is 0.080 ... The re-trained FgSegNet model has a slightly better performance (0.109)'; YOLO/MaskRCNN 'could not detect any under water objects'
C_EV: no statement found (no score threshold reported)
E_EV: Sec. IV: only foreground-segmentation IoU scores reported (FgSegNet 0.080/0.109, GMM 0.186, kNN 0.125)
ARCH: FgSegNet (pre-trained and re-trained), GMM, kNN background subtraction; off-the-shelf YOLO, Mask R-CNN, Google Vision AI
NOTE: Short dataset paper with pilot experiments. Off-the-shelf models trained on non-underwater data (CDnet/ImageNet/COCO) tested on observatory footage -> R1=Y; R3=Y based on pre-trained (0.080) vs re-trained (0.109) IoU on same data, but re-training split undescribed - verifier check. Observatory measures turbidity/chlorophyll but no values reported for the dataset (V1=NR). V3=Y on basis of time-of-day selection (borderline). PRE coded COCO for off-the-shelf YOLO/MaskRCNN ('trained using ImageNet and/or COCO').
